effect: The kidneys, ureters and bladder are connected; I can now follow how the kidneys process blood.
reason: The blood sample is shown approaching the filter in the nephron preparation.

effect: The sample shows that water and small substances enter the tubule while blood cells and most proteins remain in the blood. The next step is to recover useful substances.
reaction: The distinction between what passes through and what stays in the blood is clear.
reason: The selective tubule transporters are positioned to move substances from the filtered fluid toward the blood.
expectation: The transporters will return useful dissolved substances to the blood.

effect: Useful substances, including almost all filtered glucose in healthy kidneys, have been recovered. Water recovery is the next apparent step.
reaction: The distinction between filtering and selectively recovering substances is useful.
reason: The water-permeable tubule is shown moving water from the tubule toward nearby blood vessels.
expectation: Some water will return from the filtered sample to the blood.

effect: Water has returned to the blood while wastes remain in the tubule, leaving the sample ready for drainage.
reaction: The sequence from filtration to recovery is clear.
reason: The urinary drainage leads from the kidney toward the ureter and bladder, so it is the apparent next route for the remaining fluid.
expectation: The remaining fluid will enter the urinary drainage route as urine.

effect: The remaining fluid is now shown as urine moving to the bladder, completing the filtering and recovery goal. The urinary organs still need to be connected to the body.
reaction: The sequence is clear, though the drainage step was predictable.
reason: The assembled kidney pair has ureters and a bladder, and the remaining goal is to connect the urinary organs to the body.
expectation: The urinary organs will connect to the body's circulation and other structures.

effect: Connecting the kidneys, ureters and bladder to the body completed the remaining goal and showed the kidneys linked to circulation.
reaction: The final connection brought the separate filtering sequence back into the larger body model.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering the blood sample and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile. The sequence made clear that filtration does not simply remove wastes: useful substances enter the tubule too and must be reclaimed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the ureters and bladder was clear but predictable; those fittings offered little decision-making beyond matching the named slots.

surprise.text: I found it useful that almost all filtered glucose is normally recovered in healthy kidneys, after the filter initially lets many small substances through.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The item descriptions and goal gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in continuing to see how another system connects to the body, although the predictable matching leaves me wanting more meaningful choices.
